task: fixed-window local zoom diagnostic, no retraining

window.rgb_zoom: bilinear 196 to 392, align_corners=False, from RGB in [0, 1]
window.rgb_then: ImageNet normalize after zoom; normalized tensors are not zoomed
window.map_paste: 28x28 two-group mean distance, bilinear to 196, align_corners=True

postprocess.global_only: 28x28 two-group mean cosine distance -> bilinear 392 align_corners=True -> bilinear 256 align_corners=False -> conv gaussian kernel 5x5 sigma=4
postprocess.official_equivalence: scored global map uses bottle_sep_b6.cal_anomaly_maps (interpolate each group to 392, then mean). This is the linear equivalent of averaging the two 28x28 distances first.
postprocess.local_only: fused 392 map -> bilinear 256 align_corners=False -> same gaussian
postprocess.fused: 0.5 * global_392 + 0.5 * local_392, then the same 256 resize and gaussian. No per-image min-max.

image_auroc_note: Computed once from global_only. Score is the mean of the highest 1% pixels on the final 256 gaussian map.

region_definition.structure: 9x9 all ones, one erosion and one dilation, origin centered
region_definition.average: micro-average over pooled pixels, including good images where the dilation is empty

global_only.pixel_f1_max_note: threshold selected on the test set; optimistic
global_only.defect_recall_at_normal_fpr_definition: Linear interpolation on the pixel ROC. FPR is the false-positive rate among gt==0 pixels. Recall is the true-positive rate among gt==1 pixels. The operating FPR is exactly the named value. Higher score is more anomalous.
